One Man Cost Banks $10 Billion. Nobody Saw His Name
In March 2021, a family office most investors had never heard of cost the world's banks more than ten billion dollars in days. How did Bill Hwang hide it, and why did the banks let him? This documentary follows Bill Hwang from Tiger Management and the 2012 Tiger Asia guilty plea to Archegos, the family office that used total return swaps to keep its positions off public filings. Argentina Defaulted 9 Times. Then Got a $57 BILLION IMF Deal
Argentina was once one of the richest countries on Earth. Then came nine sovereign defaults. Why does the same debt crisis keep coming back? This documentary traces Argentina's debt cycle: the export boom and the early defaults, Perón's state expansion, the 1976 military regime's borrowing, the 1991 Convertibility peg and the 2001 collapse, the holdout fight with Paul Singer's NML Capital and the pari passu ruling, the 2018 IMF agreement, and Javier Milei's 2023 fiscal shock. Brazil 2022: The Runoff Decided by 2.1 Million Votes
On October 30, 2022, Brazil held the closest presidential runoff in its modern democratic history. Out of more than 124 million ballots cast on electronic voting machines across 5,570 municipalities, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated incumbent President Jair Bolsonaro by 2,139,645 votes—50.90% to 49.10%. WeWork: How a $47 Billion Startup Ended in Bankruptcy
In 2019, WeWork was valued at $47 billion. Four years later, it filed for bankruptcy. How did an office-rental company convince the world it was a tech giant — and what was really hiding inside its leases? This documentary traces WeWork from a New York coworking startup to SoftBank's biggest bet, the failed 2019 IPO, the pandemic, the 2021 SPAC listing, the 2023 Chapter 11 filing and its 2024 emergence from bankruptcy.
